title: Capacity margin tracker + risk matrix — weekly sync 2026-08-24
body:
Weekly sync notes: capacity margin tracker and operational risk matrix

Date: 2026-08-24
Attendees: Aisha P., Ben O., Lina G., Markus T., Priya S., oncall rotation (Carlos R.)
Meeting length: 45m (standup + focused deep-dive)
Purpose: Reconcile current fleet margin across regions, surface near-term risks for next 7–14 days, and assign mitigations. This doc is working notes + action list to drive next steps.

Summary:
- Net available GPU margin across all regions stands at ~8.4% against committed SLA-backed demand. Margin trend: down 2.3ppt week-over-week due to higher Hosted API tail and a batch scheduling change in us-west.
- APAC preemptible churn spike (3× typical) last 48h; investigation points to two new cloud maintenance windows overlapping our low-latency pools. Short-term mitigation: migrate burst jobs to eu-west reserve and increase prewarm allocation on edges.
- EU-west now has a soft reservation tied to two enterprise Dedicated customers (contracted, but on flexible start). If they ramp, margin would drop to ~1.1% there.
- Actionable risks prioritized in the matrix below.

Key metrics (rolling 7d):
- Total fleet GPUs (logical): 14,820
- Committed SLA demand (95th percentile peak tokens/sec equivalent): 13,585 GPUs
- Active reserved + pinned (Dedicated): 5,200 GPUs
- Available shared pool (hosted/burstable): 6,035 GPUs
- Global margin = (available - forecasted buffer) / committed = 8.4%
- Preemption incidents last 7d: 12 (APAC=7, US-W=3, EU=2)

Per-region snapshot (current + forecast):
- us-west: total 4,600 | reserved 1,400 | shared 2,600 | margin 9.0% | note: batch placement change on 8/22 increased latency tail for the shared pool; scheduler adjustment (PR linked) throttled batch size to improve latency — which squeezed throughput.
- us-east: total 3,500 | reserved 900 | shared 2,000 | margin 7.8% | note: stable, but busy evenings (customer A ramping).
- eu-west: total 3,200 | reserved 1,800 (soft) | shared 1,000 | margin 1.1% if soft reserved customers start ramping | note: high risk window 2026-08-28..2026-09-03 for Dedicated onboarding.
- apac (multi-zone): total 3,520 | reserved 100 | shared 435 | preemptible 2,985 | margin 13.4% nominal but volatile due to preemptible churn. Planned maintenance windows increase preemption probability.

Risk matrix (prioritized):
1) EU onboarding ramp conflicts with SLA-backed routes (Likelihood: Medium-High, Impact: High)
   - Mitigation: offer temporary cross-region routing to us-west + brief EU burst credits; enable canary throttles for the enterprise tenants. Owner: Priya S. Due: 2026-08-26
2) APAC preemptible maintenance spike causing tail-latency regressions (Likelihood: High, Impact: Medium)
   - Mitigation: toggle prewarm factor from 1.35 -> 1.6 on APAC edge pools during maintenance windows; re-route non-latency-critical burst work to eu-west reserved. Owner: Ben O. Due: immediate; implement by 2026-08-25
3) Scheduler batch-size tuning reduces token throughput unexpectedly (Likelihood: Medium, Impact: Medium)
   - Mitigation: revert recent batch-size change on canary route and run A/B with controlled traffic. Owner: Markus T. Due: 2026-08-25
4) Sudden Enterprise failover to Dedicated (uncoordinated) dropping shared margin below operational threshold (Likelihood: Low, Impact: High)
   - Mitigation: implement automated soft-threshold alerting + throttled on-ramp policy. Owner: Lina G. Due: 2026-09-02

Notes from troubleshooting (last 72h):
- Investigated 3 preemption incidents in apac-east-2; cloud provider logs indicate maintenance; ops ticket opened (JIRA-OPS-8812). Evacuation was smooth, but cold-start latency observed for a subset of requests (~420ms 95th).
- A temporary config change to scale-down autoscaling cooldowns improved cost but exposed latency spikes during short surges; reverted in staging for more tests.
- PR 1289 (runtimes) patches scheduler backpressure; running extended canary to validate throughput impact. Link in artifacts.

Decisions made in this sync:
- Increase APAC prewarm factor to 1.6 during provider maintenance windows (temporary, reevaluate in 7d).
- Add an explicit eu-west uplift buffer of 120 GPUs for the week of 8/28; finance-approved temporary credit to avoid outage for the onboarding enterprise.
- Run a controlled emergency drill on 2026-08-29 to simulate a 20% regional preemption event (US-W or APAC). Purpose: validate cross-region routing + cold-start tolerances. Organizer: Carlos R.

Action items (owner, due):
- Priya S.: Confirm enterprise onboarding schedule and gating points; add hard start date or commit to cross-region fallback. Due 2026-08-26. Linked: JIRA-CLUSTER-7421.
- Ben O.: Implement APAC prewarm factor change and add metric dashboard for preemption-induced latency. Due 2026-08-25.
- Markus T.: Pause batch-size rollout on canary routes and gather token/sec vs latency curves. Due 2026-08-25.
- Lina G.: Draft automated threshold alerting proposal and runbook snippet for on-ramp throttles. Due 2026-09-02.
- Aisha P.: Schedule emergency drill + send runbook + invite list; collect postmortem template. Due 2026-08-26.

Open questions / blockers: 
- Need clarity from Sales on exact onboarding pattern for the EU enterprise customer (burst vs steady). Pending Sales sync (Priya).
- Runbook gap: no documented steps for temporary cross-region token-bucket adjustments; create small runbook fragment and run tabletop. Owner: Aisha.

Relevant links & references:
- Confluence: Fleet margin guidelines (confluence:redwood/fleet-margin-guidelines)
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-8812 (APAC preemption), JIRA-CLUSTER-7421 (EU onboarding)
- GitHub: runtimes PR #1289 (scheduler fixes)

Quick wins to reduce risk this week:
- Apply APAC prewarm change (Ben)
- Add eu-west temporary uplift (Finance + Priya)
- Revert batch-size change on canary (Markus)

Next sync: 2026-08-31 (same time). Will present: post-drill notes, updated margin after prewarm change, and eu-west onboarding confirmation.

Notes to self: retain this doc as the working provenance for alerts and postmortem. Convert to final runbook snippet after drill.

-- end of notes --
